proposed_from.topic: Rare-exceedance cancellation geometry for normal-link distributional DiD. For the fifteen fixed pre/post pairs in the Djuazon--Tsyawo crime-free DTT aggregate, use predeclared disjoint block-role samples and write each of four exceedance probabilities as rho c_j on a fixed comparable-rarity box. Prove that the complete probit-versus-Poisson error factors as rho Q A C_rho, where A=log(c1/c3)log(c2/c3), C_rho<0, and u^2 C_rho=-1+O(u^-2) uniformly including the exact cancellation planes. Derive the pairwise and aggregate drifting-cancellation Gaussian frontier, bounded-count product-Poisson limits, and a zero-count-safe finitely terminating rational outer confidence interval with simultaneous coverage and the stated expected-diameter order. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An explicit inverse-Mills integral remainder yields the uniform mixed-derivative expansion without dividing by A. Exact-plane, opposite-sign, approaching-plane, all-zero, all-full, unequal-share, and fifteen-pair cases were checked. A rational-grid construction with an explicit global Lipschitz certificate preserves coverage and diameter order; bounded searches found no same-theorem collision. The published 37-treated-block sample forces the conservative aggregate interval to include zero, so no finite-sample power claim is made. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently prove the common-cutoff inverse-tail and mixed-derivative constants uniformly over the full coefficient box, closing K4-U on both cancellation planes. EARLY KILL TEST: Certify the mixed derivative as one log ratio tends to zero and verify all-zero retention plus the all-full empty-list output for n_j at most six; failure should pivot or stop. proposed_from.novelty_justification: Djuazon and Tsyawo's normal-link counterfactual identity is treated only as the published causal baseline, and the displayed interior influence-function result is only a split-role specialization of their Theorem 2(c). Their Assumption 5 requires \(\inf_{g,t,y}\phi(\Phi^{-1}(F_{gt}(y)))\ge1/C\); under \(F=\rho_n c\) with \(\rho_n\to0\), this density converges to zero, so the comparable-rarity arrays are outside their theorem. The closest analytic result is Pinelis's inverse-Mills derivative control. Neither comparator gives the mixed coefficient \(C_{\rho,\ell}\), the exact factorization \(\Delta_{\ell}-\Delta^P_{\ell}=\rho Q_{\ell}A_{\ell}C_{\rho,\ell}\), uniformity on the two cancellation planes, the associated Gaussian and product-Poisson frontier, or the rational outer-inference result.

proposed_from.literature_map: Djuazon and Tsyawo (2026), at Theorem 1 and equation (5), identify the three-input transformed-CDF counterfactual; their proof in Section S.1.1 is algebraic identification, while Theorem 2 uses an interior functional delta method under Assumption 5. Their Section 5 averages fifteen admissible comparisons and uses a block bootstrap for the crime application, whose treated arm contains 37 blocks. Pinelis (2019), at the main theorem and derivative corollary, obtains exact inverse-Mills bounds through non-asymptotic stationary-phase integral representations, but does not study a mixed distributional-DiD finite difference. Baricz (2008), in Sections 2--3, proves monotonicity, complete monotonicity, and Turán inequalities for the Gaussian Mills ratio; these results motivate a sign certificate but do not yield the proposed two-direction factorization. Chen and Fang (2019), at their second-order delta theorem and bootstrap iff theorem, treat zero first derivatives in a Gaussian base experiment; bounded rare counts lie outside that experiment. Marohn (2001) separates Gaussian and Poisson limits for truncation experiments, without a causal DiD map or cancellation drift. Sachs, Gabriel, and Fay (2026), in their exact null inversion and Monte Carlo algorithm, cover arbitrary continuous multinomial functionals at finite samples, but the exact continuum computation is infeasible and their implementation approaches the exact p-value from below. Fernández-Val, Meier, van Vuuren, and Vella (2024) use nonlinear distribution regression and explicit tail restrictions, but do not state a common-rarity normal-versus-Poisson coefficient. Roth and Sant'Anna (2023) show that functional-form sensitivity is identifying content, not cosmetic specification choice. Searches through these cited and citing threads found no closer result subsuming the exact coefficient, its two cancellation planes, both rare-count limit branches, and a deterministic rational outer interval.
